chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: Defining jazz as rhythmic improvisation
summary: Wooding says jazz is improvisation plus a rhythmic pattern on any melody, and Black players excel because of rhythm.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Was there any improvisation involved in what you played over there?
Yeah, but we didn't have too much over there.

You see, because really, that's what jazz is. It's the rhythmic improvisation on any piece. You can take -- I know, years before that, I think I told you there was a fellow by the name of Duke, and he took "Onward Christian Soldiers". When they got through with it, swinging it with the stride, like he used to, like he used to play like that. And the improvisation is when you don't give a note all its beats, you see? You cut it short, like, (sings), you know what I mean?
It's the improvisation plus the rhythmic
pattern that you put to any melody. You can play anything you want. And that's all that jazz is really, that is.

And the reason why we are in the front in it is because we have more rhythm than the other groups, the blacks do. That's the only reason why. It isn't that we are creating anything more than anybody else, but it's the rhythmic effect.
